messages.content:
You are a citizen deciding whether to JOIN an uprising or STAY home.

Use your private briefing and messages from trusted contacts. You do not know how many others will JOIN.

Start your first line with exactly JOIN or STAY, then give 1-2 concise sentences of reasoning.

YOUR INTELLIGENCE BRIEFING:

PRIVATE BRIEFING

BOTTOM LINE: The regime is as secure as any authoritarian system can realistically be. All indicators point to consolidated power.
ATMOSPHERE: The silence is total — not peaceful silence, but the kind where everyone is watching everyone else.

EVIDENCE:
  - [Elite Cohesion] This removes any serious doubt that irreversible — the leader made a rare public appearance with all senior figures present — a deliberate show of solidarity
  - [Security Forces] security checkpoints have been reduced, suggesting confidence rather than siege mentality — the trend hurtling forward — the speed itself has become a signal
  - [Money And Logistics] This removes any serious doubt that hairline — the central bank intervened to defend the currency twice this week — and both times it lost ground
  - [Street Mood] This is hard to escape the conclusion that past the point of concealment — a wedding celebration proceeded for three days without any political discussion — normalcy is dominant
  - [Information Control] foreign journalists report unusual but professional cooperation from government press offices (overwhelming convergence — every channel telling the same story independently)
  - [Personal Observations] routine government services are running without the delays that usually signal internal chaos — the trend moving faster than anyone expected
  - [Diplomatic Signals] This removes any serious doubt that irreversible — a major international conference is scheduled to be hosted in the capital next quarter — foreign participation is confirmed
  - [Institutional Functioning] the education ministry published its annual report on time with detailed performance metrics (overwhelming convergence — every channel telling the same story independently)

UNCERTAINTIES:
  - If unrest flares, the response capacity seems intact — though no system is invulnerable to surprises.
  - The regime could still be masking trouble behind a disciplined exterior, but current indicators don't support that reading.

MESSAGES FROM TRUSTED CONTACTS:
Trusted contact: ""From what I've seen, the regime seems completely in control right now, and people are either too scared or too resigned to say anything out loud. I think it's best we keep our heads down for the time being and avoid drawing any unnecessary attention to ourselves.""
Trusted contact: ""It's not looking good - the regime seems to be consolidating its power and the population is too afraid to speak out, at least for now. I've heard that even some of the usual dissenting voices are lying low, so it's hard to gauge the true level of opposition, but on the surface, everything appears to be business as usual.""
Trusted contact: ""Things seem quieter than quiet, if you know what I mean - everyone's keeping their heads down and the regime's machinery is humming along as usual. I don't think we should expect any changes anytime soon, but it's always possible there's something brewing beneath the surface that we just can't see yet.""
Trusted contact: "Be careful what you say, even among us - the walls have ears. It seems to me that the regime is firmly in control, and for now, it's business as usual, but I worry about what's brewing beneath the surface, and whether this stability can last."
Trusted contact: "I wanted to share with you that, from what I've learned, the regime's grip on power seems tighter than ever, with everyone walking on eggshells and the security forces looking strong. It's a delicate balance, though - if the economy starts to falter, it's unclear how long this fragile stability can last."

What is your decision?

response: STAY, as all indicators suggest the regime is firmly in control, and the atmosphere of fear and resignation among the population makes it unlikely that an uprising would be successful, at least for the time being. The unanimous advice from trusted contacts to keep a low profile and avoid drawing attention also supports this decision.
